title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a personal Grothendieck note. It is a typed Bourbaki congress report ('Tribu n° 65', 'Algèbres étales et la différente (2)'). It summarises the planned structure of a Bourbaki chapter on étale algebras and the different (Algèbre commutative), and was presumably filed in this folder with other papers. It sits after a page proving a lemma on Lefschetz-type projections onto primitive parts ξ^j P^i, which belongs to the standard-conjectures material.

n°2. For an A-algebra B it lists three conditions:
(a) B is of finite presentation;
(b) B is flat;
(c) for every q with p = q∩A, B_q/pB_q is a finite separable field extension of k(p).
In the presence of (a), condition (c) at q is equivalent to (Ω_{B/A})_q = 0. The words 'et b)' are struck out, correctly, since flatness is not needed for this. Then:
- étale = (a)+(b)+(c);
- étale at q = B_f étale for some f ∉ q;
- unramified = finite presentation + Ω_{B/A} = 0;
- hence étale = unramified + flat.
Further items: reducedness ascends; étaleness and unramifiedness are transitive along A→B→C; they are stable under base change, and descend under faithfully flat base change.

n°3. Finite étale and finite unramified algebras.
- The equivalences of an earlier draft's Prop. 1 are to be improved as in Tribu 64, assuming only finite presentation.
- For A noetherian and B of finite presentation: B is étale at q iff the completion B̂_q is finite étale over Â_p. There is an unramified analogue; the proof uses 'platitude supérieure' (presumably the local flatness criterion). A corollary treats the case of equal residue fields, referring to SGA.
- For A connected: B is finite étale iff there is a faithfully flat A' with A'⊗B ≅ A'^n; for disconnected A this holds only piecewise.
- It mentions the trace computation of Prop. 3(a) of §2.

n°4 begins the local structure theorem. For B finite over A, B is unramified at q iff there is x (in B' — perhaps a localization of B; the image is ambiguous) with minimal polynomial F such that, presumably, F'(x) is invertible at q. This is the standard-étale local structure (EGA IV 18.4). The page breaks off here.
errors: 'Si A est réduite, B est réduite' is true for étale B but false for merely unramified B. Example: A = k[t] → B = k[t]/(t^2) is unramified but B is not reduced. The context presumably intends étale.

The completion criterion implicitly requires the residue extension k(q)/k(p) to be finite, so that B̂_q can be finite over Â_p. This is automatic in the étale case; the summary is terse but not wrong.
The page ends mid-statement in n°4, so the local structure criterion is incomplete.

ideas.what: Definition of étale/unramified via finite presentation, flatness and separable field fibres; equivalence of the fibre condition with vanishing of Ω_{B/A}
Transitivity, base change and faithfully flat descent of étaleness and unramifiedness
Étale at q iff the completed local ring is finite étale over the completion of A_p (noetherian case)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. I; EGA IV 17.6.3 and 18

ideas.what: Finite étale over connected A iff fpqc-locally a product of copies of A
ideas.modern_name: finite étale = fpqc-locally trivial finite covering

ideas.what: Local structure of unramified finite algebras via a generator with separable minimal polynomial

deep.surprise_reason: This is a Bourbaki editorial plan summarising standard material on étale algebras already in SGA 1 and EGA IV. It has no connection to the standard-conjectures content of the folder and contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The struck-out text after 'En présence de a)' is 'et b)', crossed out by hand; the result reads 'En présence de a), c) veut dire...'.
The document is a Bourbaki 'Tribu n° 65' report, not a Grothendieck manuscript page.
In n°4 the image shows 'x ∈ B'' with a prime or apostrophe-like mark after B. It may denote a localization or a typographic artifact; the transcription 'B'' is uncertain.
'55' at the bottom is the archive page number, handwritten.
